latest_release.name: SkillEvaluator 0.9.0
latest_release.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.9.0

SkillEvaluator 0.9.0 expands how you build evaluation datasets, compare skill versions, and understand why an agent passed or failed. It adds controls for evaluation budgets, reusable baselines, and clearer evidence across terminal, HTML, JSON, Markdown, and benchmark reports.

For PyPI users upgrading from 0.7.2, this release also includes the changes shipped in the GitHub-only 0.8.0 release.

## Highlights

- **Build and review better evaluation datasets.** Declare deterministic checks for script execution, workspace files, and final responses. Generate datasets grounded in skill instructions, author intent, or traces; import production traces as redacted review candidates; and promote expectations only after explicit human review. Preview legacy dataset migrations before writing a new file.
- **Track skill improvements over time.** Compare retained skill versions with `--compare-to` and `compare-versions`, browse run history, and reuse a compatible no-skill baseline with `--reuse-baseline`. Version comparisons remain separate from Skill Lift against a no-skill baseline.
- **Control evaluation spending.** Set token, judge-call, attempt, and priced-cost budgets. Reports retain partial results when limits stop a run. Token usage is shown per case and agent, with missing counters and reused-baseline usage identified.
- **Understand the evidence behind each result.** Reports show met, unmet, unchecked, and inapplicable expectations; dataset coverage and sufficiency; skill activation; failed-arm coverage; and concrete next steps. Skill Lift is the headline comparison, with pass@k shown as supporting reliability. HTML charts work offline.
- **Audit graders and judge decisions.** Qualify the shipped verifier with `tier3 validate-grader`, inspect retained judge requests and replies, use opt-in judge retry and fallback policies, and ask questions about a completed run with `tier3 feedback`. Import externally computed custom metrics with their provenance.
- **Extend repository CI.** Opt-in GitHub and GitLab setup adds advisory Tier 2 and Tier 3 evaluations alongside required Tier 1 checks. Capability-gated onboarding supports independent chat, judge, and agent models, reviewed scanner baselines, retained benchmark cards, and optional trusted feedback.

## Notable fixes

- Align Skill Lift, dimension applicability, verdicts, and publication status across report formats. Failed baselines are labeled incomplete rather than “not run,” and missing evidence stays visible.
- Improve Tier 2 handling of large repeated-content clusters, malformed LLM verdicts, collection coverage, and shell-script chunking. Failed catalog rebuilds preserve the previously committed registry.
- Reduce security and PII false positives while retaining real coverage gaps and scanner failures. Dependency advisories now appear as structured findings in reports and SARIF; stable finding IDs support tracking across runs.
- Improve agent setup retries, cancellation, stop-on-pass concurrency, UTF-8 dataset loading, retained feedback, and Docker setup. Upgrade the Tier 3 backend to Harbor 0.25.0.

## Upgrade considerations

- **Dataset generation now defaults to `auto` grounding.** Provide substantive author guidance or usable matching traces. Skill-only starter flows need `--grounding skill`, including with `--no-llm`. Older datasets that require skill use may need outcome-only expectations to pass strict CI validation; the no-skill baseline receives the same checks.
- **Some grading outcomes change.** Accuracy evaluates task outcomes without penalizing a no-skill baseline for not identifying the skill. Standard judge scores are computed from verdicts. A scored attempt fails when goal accuracy or security is below 1.0; a scored dimension below 0.40 fails the Tier 3 verdict even when another dimension has no score. Re-evaluate before comparing scores with older releases.
- **Baseline timeout tolerance is opt-in.** `--tolerate-baseline-timeouts` appl

# SkillEvaluator ![SkillEvaluator wordmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/skillevaluator-wordmark.svg) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%20%7C%203.13%20%7C%203.14-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Documentation-docs.nvidia.com-blue.svg)](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2608.20614-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614) [![NVIDIA Developer Blog](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blog-NVIDIA%20Developer-76B900.svg)](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/) > 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI) SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and measures their effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill. Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Get started Three ways in, one CLI, same results.
1. Run the CLI directly 2. Add it to your repo via CI 3. Wire it to your agent
Install (or `uv tool install`): ```bash pip install skillevaluator ``` Run all Tier 1 checks, no API key: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill --tiers 1 ``` Or run from a clone: [Quickstart](#quickstart). Check changed skills on every pull request. On GitHub, run: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` It opens a setup PR. On GitLab, copy the [CI template](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/tree/main/ci/bundles/0.9.0). Add the [SkillEvaluator skill](skills/skillevaluator/) to Claude Code, Codex or any skill-aware agent: ```bash npx skills add \ NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator ``` Then ask: *"Is my skill any good?"* No Node.js? [Copy the folder](docs/agent-skill.mdx#install).
Guides: [installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation), [CI setup](docs/cli-onboarding.mdx) ([GitHub](docs/github-actions.mdx), [GitLab](docs/gitlab-ci.mdx), [report examples](ci/examples/README.md)) and [agent skill](docs/agent-skill.mdx). ## Quickstart Both paths use bundled `text-analyzer`. | Start here | Requires | First result | | --- | --- | --- | | [Run without an LLM](#run-without-an-llm) | Git and uv | A deterministic quality score and findings | | [Use NVIDIA Build](#use-nvidia-build) | Git, uv, and a Build API key | Model-backed rubric scores and feedback | Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git, then get the example: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git cd SkillEvaluator ``` uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies. For standalone installation, see [Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). ### Run without an LLM ```bash uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality ``` No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores **84.5/100 (B)**, exits `0` and saves `reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json`. The passing threshold defaults to 70. This checks static quality; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path with your skill directory. See the [keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm). ### Use NVIDIA Build Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for **free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product). 1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment. 2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key. 3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check: ```bash export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...' uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build ``` The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in `reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json`. No agent runtime or Docker is needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds. The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the [Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) or [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx). ## Three-tier overview ![SkillEvaluator three-tier pipeline: Skill → Tier 1 Validation → Tier 2 Deduplication → Tier 3 Live Evaluation → Reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/three-tier-overview.svg) Each tier is independent. Add its extra to your command: | Tier | Question | Example after setup | Additional setup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Tier 1: Validation | Is the skill safe and well-formed? | `uv run skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm` | External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks | | Tier 2: Deduplication | Does guidance repeat or overlap? | `uv run --extra tier2 skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill` | Embeddings and chat; add `--catalog ./skill-catalog.json` for inter-skill comparison | | Tier 3: Live Evaluation | Does the skill help the agent? | `uv run --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill` | Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default) | Tier 1 fetches pinned, verified SkillSpector and Gitleaks releases when they are missing; Semgrep is optional. See [scanners](docs/installation.mdx#system-tools). `--no-llm` does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is `INCOMPLETE` and exits nonzero. [SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) provides specialized skill security scanning; [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor), the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs. Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See [tier guides](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/). ## Run the combined pipeline After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers: ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator validate ./my-skill ``` `doctor` checks readiness, not inference success. `validate` runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use `--tiers 1,2` to skip live evaluation or `--tiers 1` for static checks. `--no-autopilot` requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages. Tier 1 gates `validate`. Tier 2 gates unless `--no-block-on-dedup` is set; Tier 3 gates only with `--block-on-agent-eval`. Model and managed-sandbox usage can incur charges; see [runtime and cost](docs/tier3-live-evaluation.mdx#plan-for-cost). Standalone generation needs substantive `evals/EVAL.md` guidance, a `--prompt` file with task requests and outcomes, or matching retained traces. `--force` below replaces the autopilot starter; `--refine` refines it. Explicit `--grounding skill` permits skill-only starters. Review cases; templates omit unauthored negatives. ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full --prompt eval-guidance.md --force ``` ## Run from a source checkout Use `uv run --python 3.13` with the relevant extra. See [Installation](docs/installation.mdx#choosing-extras) for extras and standalone upgrades. ## Research and citation Resources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614), [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20614), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.20614), [BibTeX](https://arxiv.org/bibtex/2608.20614), and the [NVIDIA Developer blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/). Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff). ## Documentation See [the documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) for setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and [performance dashboard](docs/reports.mdx#performance-dashboard). ## Installation and third-party software Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation) to choose the full installation or a smaller per-tier setup. This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use. ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run: ```bash make lint && make test && make build ``` See [project governance](GOVERNANCE.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Support Support level: **Experimental**. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues); see [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md). ## Security Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub issue. ## Releases Release changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/releases). ## License Apache License 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
